decisions.reason: As a niche but still closely related reusable crate for agriculture, it fits the firm's existing packaging knowledge well enough that management would likely keep it and use early market feedback to refine it rather than withdraw it quickly.
A foldable large container sits squarely in the firm's core returnable-packaging competence and its dedicated web presence suggests enough strategic commitment to continue learning and improving it.
A stackable plastic crate is highly aligned with the firm's established product architecture and manufacturing know-how, so the firm has strong absorptive capacity to support and adapt it.

A medium-duty rackable pallet is a core-adjacent logistics product that the firm can readily evaluate and optimize through its engineering and customer relationships, making retention more likely than exit.

Although more specialized, the spill-retention pallet builds on the firm's pallet and industrial-packaging expertise, and its own web page indicates a serious commercialization effort worth continuing.

This plastic pallet with load retainers is strongly connected to the firm's existing pallet platform and customer use cases, so management would likely keep it while leveraging in-house development to improve adoption.
